note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent judge, authored none of gap #55: 3c2c96ec01, c7a04ba492, 41e11adf5c, a0d9424aa6, eaaf43bbf8, da45187adf, 6e810d411b, 57c4c5d6eb, 96caad6102, 5ec09d6ab1). Section 8.1: "Interfaces to unnumbered point-to-point networks have no associated IP address.  On these interfaces, the IP source should be set to any of the other IP addresses belonging to the router.  For this reason, there must be at least one IP address assigned to the router." Producers read: iface unnumbered.go resolveUnnumbered/pickDonorAddress take an address another configured interface (usually loopback) owns and add it as a /32 to the unnumbered unit, refusing a missing, disabled, unnumbered or address-less donor at commit; unnumbered_donor.go reconcileUnnumbered installs the /32 only while the donor address sits on an up non-borrower device and removes it otherwise. OSPF transport backend_linux.go::interfaceIPv4 sources from that /32 (the donor address) and refuses a device with no IPv4 address; multicastDevice names the device by ifindex with the donor as Address, so IP_MULTICAST_IF and the AllSPFRouters membership land on the unnumbered device, not the donor device that holds the same address. Positive TestOSPFUnnumberedSourcesFromDonorAddress (guest, integration): device holds only the donor /32 (the form iface installs), donor on a dummy; asserts getsockopt IP_MULTICAST_IF == donor, the peer reads the IP header source == donor with the exact payload, and the peer's reply to AllSPFRouters arrives on the unnumbered device. Mutant record (multicastDevice ifindex->0) is current per ./le rfc check. Negative TestOSPFRefusesDeviceWithoutRouterAddress: a namespace with no IPv4 address anywhere, kernel control proves the AllSPFRouters join succeeds without one, the backend still refuses and names the missing address; mutant record (interfaceIPv4 error->nil) is current. rp_filter: the positive sets loose (2) on the unnumbered end and 0 on all and the device in the peer namespace. This does not weaken the 8.1 proof: rp_filter acts only on the receiver's acceptance, the source Ze's kernel writes is unchanged by it, and the test compares that source to the donor exactly, so a wrong source still fails. What the guest test does not show is that a strict-filtering neighbor with no route to the donor accepts the Hellos; that is a deployment property, documented in docs/guide/ospf.md, and ospf-p2p-unnumbered-frr covers the realistic shape (FRR loose rp_filter with a default route out the link, no rp_filter 0) where FRR lists Ze's neighbor by the donor 10.255.0.2, reaches Full, and both sides route to the other's donor over eth0. Whole stack: config `ipv4 unnumbered zeloop` -> /32 on eth0 -> OSPF source = donor is exercised by that interop scenario; the guest test hand-installs the /32 rather than going through iface config. Scope note (no verdict change): Ze treats a link as unnumbered only when iface declares it; a device carrying no address and no `ipv4 unnumbered` is refused rather than sourced from some other router address, which still meets the sentence for every link Ze runs unnumbered. Not observed by this judge: the two guest units SKIP on this host (CAP_NET_RAW unavailable); their red/green rests on the recorder's guest records, which ./le rfc check reports current. Host unit tests of iface, ospf, ospf/spf, ospf/lsdb pass at HEAD.
